en: If you hear thunder during a storm, you are close enough to be struck by lightning and must seek indoor shelter immediately.
During an earthquake, you should drop to the ground, take cover under a sturdy table, and hold on until the shaking stops.
Washing your hands with soap after playing in soil removes harmful parasites like hookworm larvae that can enter through your skin.
Boiling tap water for at least one minute kills harmful bacteria like cholera, making it safe to drink.
The mineral fluorite provides fluoride, which is added to toothpaste to strengthen your tooth enamel and prevent cavities.
The Sun emits ultraviolet radiation that can cause sunburns and skin cancer, so you must wear sunscreen when outside.
If you get lost at night in the Northern Hemisphere, you can find true north by locating the bright star Polaris.
The Moon's gravity causes high tides that can create dangerous rip currents, so always swim near a lifeguard during high tide.
Drinking plenty of water during hot, humid weather prevents heatstroke, a dangerous condition where your body temperature rises too high.
Before a typhoon hits, you should pack an emergency kit with bottled water, non-perishable food, and a battery-powered radio.
Loose rocks and soil on steep mountain slopes can trigger deadly landslides during heavy rains, so avoid camping in those areas.
Emptying stagnant water from tires and cans stops mosquitoes from breeding, which prevents the spread of the deadly dengue virus.
